citations.quote: No closure-under-prefixes assumption is imposed on $T$.
Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
Every ordinal $\alpha \in \omega_1$ is at most countable

derivations.claim: Omega_1 is regular; countable unions of nonstationary sets are nonstationary; limit points of an unbounded set form a club; diagonal intersection proves pressing down.
inputs: a regressive value b(alpha) is below alpha and is therefore tested by the diagonal club

derivations.claim: Countable equal-column fibers can be collapsed and increasingly reindexed without changing T_c or the coloring hypotheses; finite strings are countable.
inputs: an uncountable constant column contradicts strong unboundedness

derivations.claim: Every stationary subset of omega_1 partitions into omega_1 stationary pieces by the countable enumeration matrix.
inputs: fixed-coordinate value fibers are disjoint; one coordinate occurs uncountably often

derivations.claim: Countable cofinal ladders define finite decreasing walks and a natural-valued maximum map e.
inputs: a decreasing ordinal sequence cannot be infinite; a cofinal omega-ladder has finite proper initial segments

derivations.claim: Walk concatenation beyond a finite threshold yields eventual equality below every limit beta and bounded natural sublevels at beta.
inputs: the earlier walk contributes a fixed finite maximum dominated by the first ladder of the later walk

derivations.claim: A cofinal tree family, finite-list stationary refinement, ubiquitous successor-prefix schedule and fresh-index recursion give a globally distinct matrix d.
inputs: only countably many used indices excluded from each uncountable candidate set; every selected index is at least rho

derivations.claim: Stationary z fibers and the minimum candidate formula define h and preliminary B sets with every Delta well-defined.
inputs: alpha itself is always a candidate; all compared matrix columns are distinct

derivations.claim: Different matrix-column pairs give B intersections bounded in the smaller limit index.
inputs: above one majorant bound Delta exceeds the first column difference and equals that difference for the other column

derivations.claim: Finite unions retain bounded intersections; removing finitely many earlier row members gives disjoint A members with only bounded loss.
inputs: equal-column h fibers with different colors are disjoint; finite unions of bounded subsets of a limit are bounded

derivations.claim: Target-cylinder sets V_j lie in T_c and select a finite-list stationary piece suited to the prescribed targets.
inputs: removing countably many small prefix fibers leaves uncountably many distinct selected column indices

derivations.claim: Failure of simultaneous guessing gives one fixed failing pair and a stationary family whose preliminary target intersections share a bound b.
inputs: countable stationary completeness and the local pressing-down argument

derivations.claim: A club of target-cylinder limit points and coherence yield gamma<delta, a common threshold and an uncountable family with fixed nu-prefix.
inputs: gamma is in the stationary z-fiber of the failed row member

derivations.claim: Strong unboundedness produces n>=nu, xi above the bounded sublevel set, and a column alpha with Delta=n satisfying the B inequality.
inputs: t belongs to T_j subset V_j; gamma is a limit point of X_j^t; selected next value exceeds both e(xi,delta) and d_xi,0(n)

derivations.claim: Gamma is exactly the first candidate of h, so xi lies in the forbidden B intersection above b; simultaneous finite-target guessing follows.
inputs: every earlier candidate would lie in G above xi; the candidate gamma has e(gamma,alpha)=nu<=n

derivations.claim: Each nongood row can be replaced by split cofinal omega-ladders along indices with Delta to its anchor column tending to infinity.
inputs: every anchor prefix is in T-star and is scheduled cofinally below the row index

derivations.claim: Replaced rows retain cross-index boundedness; a hypothetical cofinal intersection from a replaced lower row contradicts a bounded e sublevel.
inputs: finite pigeonhole selects one upper matrix column, and eventual Delta becomes its fixed difference from the lower anchor

derivations.claim: All rows now satisfy cofinality/disjointness and bounded intersections; every earlier stationary finite-target success survives because it was already good.

boundaries.evidence: Step 3.2 uses nonempty finite lists and a nonempty T-star; step 8.1 sets the regressive bound to zero for empty intersections.
Step 2.3 sets C_0 empty but uses only nonempty walks; step 3.2 assigns one arbitrary matrix column at alpha=0; step 6.1 removes no earlier members for i=0.
Step 3.2 assigns a single entry outside E and permits lists of length one; step 11.1 uses nonemptiness of the list to infer every successful row is good.
Step 2.1 normalizes repeated columns before any Delta occurs; steps 5.1 and 6.1 distinguish equal and distinct column pairs; step 12.1 fills every nongood row.
Step 4.1 includes alpha as an unconditional minimum candidate without evaluating e(alpha,alpha); steps 3.1 and 13.1 use the smaller limit index for bounds.

Steps 2.2 and 2.3 identify simultaneous enumeration/ladder uses of AC; step 3.2 proves candidate sets uncountable before fresh selections; step 12.1 proves cofinal eligible prefixes before ladder replacement.
Step 2.1 proves old uncountable [T]_c uses uncountably many distinct columns and therefore new [T]_c is uncountable.
Step 2.1 proves uncountably many new eligible column representatives already form an uncountable subset of the old [T]_c.
